title: IV fluid tonicity

findings.where: Images 1–4 and 8–11; tonicity.jsx Dot and Panel sample-cell gradients
findings.title: Effective-solute dots miss the required contrast
findings.problem: Dot uses ink at 75% opacity over a variable teal gradient. Near the sample-cell rims, the composited contrast is approximately 3.7–4.0:1, below the project's 4.5:1 requirement. These small dots carry the concentration comparison; checking the ink token against the card background does not establish their actual contrast.
findings.fix: Give each particle a contrasting solid backing or halo, or lighten/flatten the sample-cell fill and use opaque particles. Test the composited particle/background colors at their actual positions in both themes.

findings.where: Images 1, 5, 6, 8, 12 and 13; bags step; LISTS, FLUIDS, fact 5 and corresponding descriptions
findings.title: The osmolarity table uses tonicity names
findings.problem: The table explicitly classifies in-bag osmolarity but labels its rows isotonic, hypotonic and hypertonic. Those terms were just defined by effective solutes and cell-volume effects. The in-bag qualification and dextrose explanation mitigate the problem, but the terminology still blurs the distinction being taught.
findings.fix: Use approximately iso-osmolar, hypo-osmolar and hyperosmolar for the osmolarity classification. Preserve familiar nursing-exam bag labels in a clearly identified note, separate from the fluid's effective tonicity after dextrose clearance.

assessment: Needs revision for particle contrast and osmolarity terminology. No clinical blocker identified in the tonicity content.
